candidate_relations.reason: An aneurysmal bone cyst does not explain the symmetric bilateral maxillary and mandibular pattern of cherubism.
A simple bone cyst is not a bilateral multilocular jaw process.
The symmetric multifocal jaw lesions of early childhood are not an odontogenic cyst.
A Stafne cavity is a focal static mandibular defect, unlike bilateral expansile cherubism.
Ameloblastoma is generally focal and does not fit the symmetric maxillomandibular childhood pattern.
Odontogenic keratocysts do not produce the characteristic symmetric cherubic jaw enlargement.
A mandibular odontogenic keratocyst cannot account for bilateral mandibular and maxillary lesions.
Fibrous dysplasia is a related skeletal differential but lacks the symmetric multilocular jaw pattern of cherubism.
Normal routine studies and the classic symmetric distribution do not support a brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism.
Langerhans cell histiocytosis does not typically cause symmetric expansile multilocular lesions of all jaws.
Odontogenic myxoma is a localized neoplasm rather than symmetric familial-pattern jaw disease.
Cherubism exactly matches the age, bilateral painless jaw enlargement, and multilocular lesions.
Central giant-cell granuloma resembles the lesional histology but does not capture the bilateral syndromic diagnosis of cherubism.
